description: This source file implements a license checking utility for Python packages, including parsing configuration files, fetching license info from PyPI, and verifying compliance based on configured allowed and disallowed licenses. It also provides command-line interface logic for checking project requirements.

classes.name: PackageLicense
classes.description: Data class representing a package's license information, including its name, version, license type, authorization status, and reason.

classes.name: LicenseChecker
classes.description: Main class that manages license verification, including loading configuration, retrieving package licenses, and checking compliance against allowed and disallowed licenses.

methods.name: Set[str] _parse_license_list(self, section: str, option: str)
methods.description: Parses the list of licenses from the configuration section, handling comments and whitespace.

methods.name: Dict[str,Dict[str,str]] _parse_authorized_packages(self)
methods.description: Parses the authorized packages section from the configuration, extracting package names, version specs, and comments.

methods.name: Optional[str] get_package_license_from_pypi( self, package_name: str, version: str )
methods.description: Fetches the license information of a package from the PyPI JSON API.

methods.name: Tuple[bool,str] is_license_acceptable(self, license_str: str)
methods.description: Determines if a given license string is acceptable based on configured license lists, handling special cases like BSD licenses.

methods.name: bool check_package(self, package_name: str, version: Optional[str] = None)
methods.description: Checks whether a particular package and its version have an acceptable license, considering manual overrides and cache.

methods.name: bool check_requirements(self, requirements_file: Path)
methods.description: Reads a requirements file and verifies the licenses of all listed packages.

methods.name: main()
methods.description: Entry point of the script that performs license verification for project dependencies and outputs the results or terminates with an error if non-compliant packages are found.
